title: Loose Rein review.yaml (rein-grounded-v1)
description: Two independently-digested halves. Regenerating `machine` resets `human`; a human recording a judgement must NOT make `machine` stale (plan 17.5). Every human-facing sentence is a statement with an epistemic status and evidence links — there is no free-form prose field anywhere in this document, because a sentence without a status is exactly what an AI fills in when it has no source (plan 6.8).

disposition.description: What a human may do about a gap. `accept the risk` is deliberately absent (plan 15.4); `dispute_finding` says the reviewer is wrong and carries the reason.

codeAnchor.description: Where in the committed tree a statement is grounded. The blob is checked against the actual object at that path, so an invented anchor cannot pass validation (plan 12.7).

declaredSurface.description: One `operator_surface` entry from the frozen plan, restated with the task that declared it and with the as-built identity of the paths it names.

as_built.description: The file as it ends up, named rather than copied: the blob at `binding.subject_head_sha` and its size. A diff shows the change; this is what somebody has to operate. The body is fetched from that commit on demand, so review.yaml never becomes a second copy of the repository.

allOf.description: A GENERATED machine review must carry its binding, its coverage manifest, its blind actual extraction, and its per-claim results. Making `not_generated` an explicit status rather than an emergent property of empty lists is the same rule as everywhere else: 'we did not measure' must be a state you can name, not one you infer from a missing field (plan 2.4).

effective_risk.description: The max of every risk contributor for this change (plan 13.5): the plan's claim and task risk, the deterministic signals, and what the coverage gap is worth. Recorded so the gate decision reads the same number the reviewers were given, instead of recomputing it from a diff that has since moved. A review that does not carry it is treated as `high`, never as `low`.

binding.description: What this review is a review OF. Any of these moving makes the whole machine review stale, and with it every human answer built on top of it.

tasks_digest.description: The `state.yaml` task facts the orientation brief and the residual findings were derived from. Separate from `change_digest`, which covers the committed tree minus .rein/: a task promoted from `awaiting-evidence` to `done` after a human recorded what they saw moves no other digest here, and regenerating across that used to reuse a brief the repository had since contradicted.

independence.description: Which model/provider group produced each half. A critical change requires the two to differ — reusing one session's output for both is not independence (plan 12.4).

unanswered.description: Expected claims the Comparator returned no result for. A model's answer is open-world: what came back is not evidence that nothing else exists, so the claim list is framed by the frozen plan and what is missing is filled deterministically as `unknown` rather than silently shortening the review (plan 2.4).

statements.description: The atomic statements every human-facing screen is assembled from (plan 6.8).

epistemic_status.description: `machine_inferred` is the honest label for 'an AI wrote this'. There is no status meaning 'reads plausibly'.

actual_extraction.description: What the code actually does, extracted WITHOUT the plan, the expected claims, or the implementer's own explanation (plan 12.2). Frozen as `actual_digest` before the comparator runs.

coverage.description: What the detector could and could not analyse, for the whole diff. `insufficient` means extra-behaviour counts read as 'undeterminable', never as '0' (plan 2.4).

analyzed_bytes.description: Size in bytes of the diff this manifest covers. Required: the `max_diff_bytes` budget is denominated in bytes, so a manifest without a measured value gives that budget no actual and it can never be exceeded. A review generated before the measure is regenerated, not tolerated.

detail.description: Which extension, or which analyzer went missing. `reason` is the closed vocabulary a query can aggregate; this is what a human needs to act on it, since 'register an analyzer for .psd' is only actionable if something says .psd.

analyzers.description: External analyzer name -> the digest of the executable that answered, for every analyzer whose reading is counted in `analyzed_files`. A file counted as read with nobody named is a claim no one can check afterwards (out-of-scope 11).

claims.description: Per-claim result on three separate axes. There is deliberately no single 'verified' field: integrity is a fact, semantic_support is somebody's judgement, and conformance is an observation. Collapsing them is what lets an AI's opinion be presented as a check (plan 2.1, 6.7).

assessment_basis.description: `machine_assessed` must never be rendered with the weight of the other three, nor translated as 'verified' (plan 6.7, 21.4).

extra_behaviors.description: Behaviour present in the code that no claim in the plan accounts for — the AI-invented `timeout=30` case (E2E-02). Shown before the raw diff, never after.

first_seen.description: The change this finding is a statement about. Without it a blocking finding was carried forward by id alone, so one taken against base A kept blocking a regeneration against base B — a different diff, sometimes no longer containing the code the finding named.

status.description: Where this finding is in its life. Absent means `open`. A finding used to have no state at all — it existed only as presence in the newest generated list — so "the change fixed it" and "the reviewer forgot it" were the same observation, and the policy refused both. `resolved` is not the reviewer's word: it is recorded only when every anchor the finding named no longer resolves in the committed tree, which is a fact about the code rather than an opinion about it.

resolved_at.description: The commit whose tree no longer carries the code this finding anchored to. Required with `status: resolved`, and it is what makes the resolution re-checkable later.

evidence.description: What the card is about — the Expected the plan states, the Actual a reviewer that never saw the plan read, and the gap or finding that raised it. Served with the card, always: it used to be withheld until the reviewer had recorded an unprimed guess, which put a comprehension quiz in front of the decision the gate was actually asking for.

brief.description: The gate-4 orientation: what this cycle delivered and under what conditions, derived from the SSOT by `brief.derive` and bound to `binding.subject_head_sha` like everything else here. It authors no sentence of its own — ids, paths, commands and image references only — and where it carries a sentence somebody else wrote, the confidence and the code anchor travel with it, because that was always the rule rather than the indirection through an id. An absent section reports nothing rather than reporting an empty finding.

delivered.description: Tasks whose work is in the reviewed tree, in the order the frozen plan lists them.

stack.description: Which dependency manifests and generated files moved. Their bodies are mechanical churn nobody reads; that they changed is the fact.

execution_boundary.description: Where each DoD step ran. `network` is what the executor enforced, not what the config hoped for: an `oci` profile is refused at run time unless its network profile is `none`, and a `host` profile has no boundary to report — which is what `unconfined` says.

environment_drift.description: Present only when the sandbox the evidence was produced in is not the one gate 3 approved. Gate 3 freezes config.yaml without its image pins, so rebuilding a pinned image mid-cycle — which a task that legitimately adds a dependency forces — costs no rollback. This is what that permission is paid for with: the approver signing at gate 4 is told, rather than left to find out.

requirements_on_people.description: What this change now requires of a person, sorted by whether anyone foresaw it. The operator-facing readings a blind extractor took out of the code are matched against the `operator_surface` entries a human froze at gate 3 — by category equality and path coverage, never by comparing one piece of prose to another. Ordered by decision value: what nobody declared, then what was declared and never read out, then a count of the foreseen ones.

undeclared.description: An operator-facing behaviour the code was read to have that no task declared. Nobody decided this would be somebody's job. Carried with its confidence and its anchor paths, because a reviewer's sentence separated from those is not evidence of anything.

unobserved.description: A declaration nothing was read out about: either it was not built or it could not be read, and telling those apart is the reviewer's job — which is why this says only that the reading is absent.

as_declared.description: Foreseen and present. A count, because a table of expected rows is where the two lists above go to hide; the entries travel with it for a reader who asks.

operations.description: The launch check. Absent means no step declares one; an empty `command` or `placeholder: true` means the DoD never started the deliverable — a green suite over a package that cannot boot is what this exists to make visible.

placeholder.description: The step's argv exits zero and establishes nothing (`["true"]` and its siblings — the same set `doctor.check_quality_gate` reports). A command that cannot fail is not a launch.

verification.description: How many DoD steps the gate ran, and which of them were established for no landed task at all. A step configured but established for nothing means every task's diff missed its `paths:`, or the run never got that far; the rest say the gate did what everyone already assumed, so they are a number rather than rows.

residuals.description: What is still open at the moment the gate is asked for.

accounts.description: What the last implementer said, in its own words, about a task that did NOT land — the account `rein report` has always written and nobody approving a gate has ever read. A claim, not a finding: the loop checks `touched` against the real diff separately, and this is the sentence beside that, not a verdict. Only unfinished tasks: for work that landed, the implementer's own explanation is the one input the blind extractor is forbidden to see, and putting it in front of the approver would move that priming onto the person the arrangement exists to protect.

residual_findings.description: Per-task review findings that were never resolved — the `consider` ones stop nothing by design and would otherwise die with the session that produced them. Each carries the commit and tree fingerprint it was observed against, which is NOT `subject_head_sha`: a reviewer looked at one task's worktree at one moment, and presenting that as an observation about the merged tree would be the overclaim this document exists to prevent.

review_budget.description: Exceeding a budget splits the scope; it never lengthens the screen (plan 14.10).

independenceGroup.description: Who produced one half of the review: the model the config asked for, and the one the launch reported having used. Both optional and neither inferred from the other — `group` is a configuration and `model` is a measurement, and a provider that serves a different model than it was told to is exactly the case where they disagree. `prompt_digest` is gone: it was declared here, read by the independence check, and written by nobody, and the check is settled on the model now.

group.description: `<adapter>/<model>` from config.yaml, derived rather than authored so it cannot name a separation the launch does not make.

model.description: The model id the launch reported. Absent when the adapter reports no usage — which is 'nobody measured', never 'it agreed'.

binding.description: Which machine review these answers are about. A POST carrying a stale machine_digest is refused rather than merged (plan 17.5).

expertise.description: Self-declared, per domain. High/critical work by a `partial` or `unfamiliar` reviewer needs an expert, an experiment, or a smaller scope — a general reviewer's risk acceptance is not enough (plan 14.9).

dispositions.description: Note what is absent: there is no 'accept the risk' action for a critical unknown (plan 15.4).
